questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, what should happen to the students?

options.text: They must leave the bus.
They should stay on the bus but move away from the fire.
They should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must leave the bus.
questions.explanation: If a school bus has a fire or a possible fire, the driver must get all students off the bus right away.

questions.question: A student drops something while walking to a school bus. What should the student do?

options.text: Stop and pick up the item.
Ask another student to pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick up the item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the item.
questions.explanation: If a student bends down to pick up a dropped item, the driver cannot see them. This is dangerous. Students should move to safety, get the driver's attention, and let the driver pick up the item.

questions.question: What skill will you be tested on during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Alley docking.
Weaving between cones.
Making an emergency stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alley docking.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset parking (left and right), driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be positioned at the end of a basic vehicle control skills test exercise?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: How should students board a school bus?

options.text: In a single-file line.
In pairs.
Without using the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly and in a single-file line. They should always use the handrail for safety.

questions.question: When can a school bus have its doors open while driving?

options.text: When crossing railroad tracks.
When the bus needs to cool down.
When there is no vehicle next to the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: When crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: School bus doors must stay closed while the bus is moving. The only exception is when crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side.
Above the door across from the driver.
Above the emergency door at the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver's side. The driver uses it to watch the passengers inside the bus.

questions.question: What skill might you be tested on during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Swerving to avoid a hazard.
Parallel parking.
Driving straight into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel parking.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset parking (left and right), driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: How do you perform a conventional parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For conventional parallel parking, drive past the space first. Then back into it, getting the rear of your vehicle as close to the back of the space as possible. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which of these do you NOT need to check?

options.text: The power steering belt.
The water compressor belt.
The alternator belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water compressor belt.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test, you will check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts if the vehicle has them.

questions.question: What does ABS allow a driver to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
See farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) prevents the wheels from locking up. It helps the driver stay in control when braking on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When should a bus roof-mounted strobe light be used?

options.text: When visibility is poor.
All the time.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: When visibility is poor.
questions.explanation: A school bus roof-mounted strobe light should be used when visibility is limited.

questions.question: What if your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing?

options.text: You will not need to do anything about railroad crossings.
You may have to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your driving test does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how to safely cross railroad tracks at a simulated location.

questions.question: What should you do if your bus stalls on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get everyone out of the bus and move far away.
Keep everyone inside and try to wave down the train.
Keep everyone inside and wait for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone out of the bus and move far away.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone out immediately and move away from the tracks. Move at an angle away from the direction of any oncoming train.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that the engine oil is in the safe range.
Show that the oil is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is and that the oil level is in the safe range, above the refill mark. You should NOT show oil below the refill mark.

questions.question: What should a driver do when dropping off students at school?

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition when leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine to secure the bus when unloading students. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave the driver's seat. You must supervise the unloading.

questions.question: What should the overhead inside rearview mirror show?

options.text: The rear tires.
All students on the bus.
The floor of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Position the overhead mirror to see all students on the bus, including those sitting directly behind the driver. The top of the mirror should show the top of the rear window.

questions.question: When students board the bus, what should the driver NOT do?

options.text: Check mirrors for students rushing toward the bus.
Count the students and make sure all have boarded.
Allow students to board in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors for rushing students and count to ensure all students board. Students must board slowly in a single-file line, not in pairs.

questions.question: When should outside mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: Before the trip starts.
While driving.
After students board.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip starts.
questions.explanation: All mirrors should be checked and adjusted before the bus begins driving.

questions.question: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, when should you do it?

options.text: Back up before students load the bus.
Back up after all students have boarded.
Back up after half the students board.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up after all students have boarded.
questions.explanation: Do not back up the bus until all students have boarded. Watch for any late-arriving students.
